earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only wordlists (Kraft 1981), comparative overviews and a sociolinguistic survey (Bombay 2002) for Hya; no grammar or phonology exists.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic (LOT Dissertation Series 375). Utrecht: LOT.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Hya. Table 3 lists 'Hya [hya] Higi none' (no phonological source exists); sec. 6.5 says published phonologies in the Higi group exist only for Bana (Hofmann 1990) and Higi/Kamwe (Hoffmann 1965, Laver 1965, Mohrlang 1971, 1972, Barreteau 1983); tone and stress are outside the book's scope.

sources.note: Nothing; classification/location entry only: hya spoken only at Amsa, 'correspond probablement au ghyɛ dont R. Mohrlang fait un dialecte higi'; higi, psikyɛ and hya treated as three distinct languages of the 'margyi' group.
